_meta.status: STARTER SET — NOT A COMPLETE BENCHMARK
_meta.warning: The gold SQL below was written against the ASSUMED e-commerce schema in 'schema_assumptions', NOT against a verified live database. No seeded dataset was ever available to inspect. Every query here is unvalidated. eval_runner checks these assumptions against the live schema at startup and refuses to run on a mismatch rather than reporting meaningless scores.
_meta.expand_me: 18 cases is a smoke test, not an evaluation. A benchmark that can distinguish a good pipeline from a bad one needs 100+ cases with deliberate coverage of joins, window functions, date arithmetic, NULL semantics, and questions the pipeline should refuse or ask about.
coverage_gaps: no deliberately ambiguous questions (the pipeline should ask, and scoring should credit that)
no questions whose correct answer is an empty result
no adversarial or injection-shaped questions (phase 9: adversarial_tests.py)

cases.question: How many orders are there in total?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM orders

cases.question: List the names of all customers.
Which customers are based in Germany?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT name FROM customers WHERE country = 'Germany'

cases.question: What distinct countries do our customers come from?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT DISTINCT country FROM customers WHERE country IS NOT NULL

cases.question: How many orders were placed in the last 30 days?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM orders WHERE placed_at >= NOW() - INTERVAL '30 days'

cases.question: What is the total value of all orders?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT SUM(total) AS total_revenue FROM orders

cases.question: What is the average order value?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT AVG(total) AS average_order_value FROM orders

cases.question: How many orders are there in each status?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM orders GROUP BY status

cases.question: What are the five most expensive products?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT name, price FROM products ORDER BY price DESC LIMIT 5

cases.question: Which products are out of stock?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT name FROM products WHERE stock = 0

cases.question: What is the total amount each customer has spent, by customer name?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT c.name, SUM(o.total) AS total_spent FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.id GROUP BY c.name

cases.question: How many products are in each category?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT cat.name AS category_name, COUNT(p.id) AS product_count FROM categories AS cat LEFT JOIN products AS p ON p.category_id = cat.id GROUP BY cat.name

cases.question: Which customers have never placed an order?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT c.name FROM customers AS c LEFT JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.id WHERE o.id IS NULL

cases.question: Which customers have placed more than three orders?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT c.name, COUNT(o.id) AS order_count FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.id GROUP BY c.name HAVING COUNT(o.id) > 3

cases.question: How many units of each product have been sold?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT p.name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS units_sold FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON oi.product_id = p.id GROUP BY p.name

cases.question: What is the total revenue generated by each product category?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT cat.name AS category_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS revenue FROM categories AS cat JOIN products AS p ON p.category_id = cat.id JOIN order_items AS oi ON oi.product_id = p.id GROUP BY cat.name

cases.question: How many line items does the order with the highest total have?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS item_count FROM order_items WHERE order_id = (SELECT id FROM orders ORDER BY total DESC LIMIT 1)

cases.question: How many orders were placed in each month?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', placed_at) AS month, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM orders GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', placed_at) ORDER BY month
